priority.override_reason: Ranks 1 through 13 are closed by current direct-leaf frame, constructor, object-cache, direct-eval, RegExp, typed-loop admission, and primitive String-cache evidence. The fresh rank-14 profile identifies a different shared cost in a region the existing typed-loop executor already admits: each entry allocates and drops its scalar registers, boxed registers, receiver vector, inline-cache vector, and any sloppy-global sink vector. The proposed reuse is keyed only by an immutable compiled typed-loop program and is bounded for recursive entries; it has no workload, source-path, checksum, or iteration-count condition. This one-target override requires the strict target, independent controls, complete external and broad coverage, and exact Test262 gates below before retention.

mechanism.summary: Lazily create and then reuse a bounded, cleared scratch bundle per compiled typed-loop program for its scalar registers, boxed values, dense-array receivers, named-property inline caches, and guarded sloppy-global sink records, instead of allocating those vectors on every native-loop entry.
mechanism.generality: The reuse applies to every already-admitted TypedLoopProgram, but its pool is created only after a region actually enters the native tier. A bundle is taken after the existing region selection and guard checks, reset to that program's immutable register/cache counts, and returned after normal exit, deoptimization, or admission decline. Nested entries take another bounded bundle or fall back to a fresh one; no scratch state crosses program instances or changes compilation, operation selection, values, caches, writeback, deoptimization, or exception behavior. Every unsupported region retains the unchanged interpreter path.
semantic_risks: all reused scalar, boxed, receiver, inline-cache, and sloppy-global records must be reset before an entry so no prior invocation can affect values, guards, property lookup, or writes
every normal exit, deoptimization, early decline, and error-adjacent return must return owned temporary storage without retaining live JS values or borrowing it across VM execution
recursive or nested invocation of the same compiled program must never alias active scratch storage; exhausted bounded pools must preserve behavior by allocating a separate bundle
cache entries and guarded global sink identities must remain invocation-local in effect, including after mutation, direct eval, or a deoptimization boundary

profile_evidence.source: macOS sample 2026-07-28 /tmp/qjs-current-bitops-bits-in-byte-profile.sample; 200x SunSpider bitops-bits-in-byte direct-script bundle executed by the exact 6cac3f50 runtime, used only to lengthen sampling and followed by executor inspection
profile_evidence.shared_cost: The 3,707-sample profile places 897 inclusive samples in the existing typed-loop executor while the hot bitsinbyte function is invoked 89,600 times. Inspection shows every admitted entry initializes fresh Vec<Typed>, Vec<Value>, receiver, inline-cache, and optional sloppy-global vectors before executing the same program. This is distinct from prior loop-admission and VM-frame-reuse experiments: the tier already runs, but its per-entry temporary storage remains allocator-bound.
